_meta.task: Switch default content_strategy to mmr_union — and what the pre-checks found
_meta.headline: Consolidation is INERT on the current corpus. At the 0.92 default zero pairs merge; it has already eaten the available duplicates. Lowering the threshold to make it fire would be unsafe, and the obvious guard against that does not work.

threshold_sweep_pairwise_dry_run.note: dream calls consolidate() with all defaults (core.py:4666) => pairwise at 0.92 => merges nothing. The 62% fact-retention gap is real but currently fires on no rows.

cluster_safety_at_085.verdict: Cosine >= 0.85 does not mean duplicate. It is driven by shared topic and shared template. Merging at this threshold would destroy 149 distinct memories.

rejected_fix_lexical_overlap_guard.idea: Require Jaccard over distinctive (>=6 char) tokens before merging.
rejected_fix_lexical_overlap_guard.why_it_failed: It is backwards for the case it was built for. The template-driven clusters — many distinct agent reports sharing one boilerplate opening line — score HIGHEST on raw lexical overlap (0.61, 0.72, 0.86) and pass the guard untouched. What it blocks instead is legitimate paraphrase merging: an existing test fixture of three genuine restatements of one fact scores ~0.13 and was vetoed.
rejected_fix_lexical_overlap_guard.what_would_work: IDF-weighted overlap. Tokens appearing across many memories (the boilerplate) get near-zero weight; rare tokens carry the signal. Raw Jaccard weights both the same, which is the bug.

retrieval_impact_precheck.method: consolidate a prod snapshot under each strategy, replay the same 200-query real corpus at +best
retrieval_impact_precheck.verdict: mmr_union's rewritten survivors do not hurt retrieval. Weak evidence though — only ~1.5% of memories merged and no gold hash was among them.

change_made: consolidate() default content_strategy: keep_higher_recall -> mmr_union. Latent safety only: pairwise mode never reads content_strategy, and cluster mode is not on any automatic path. Correct when it next fires; no effect today.
